title: Cadence-led OKR synchronization and initiative readiness dashboard
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Leadership and cross-functional partners struggle to assess initiative readiness and alignment to company-level OKRs in the fortnightly planning cadence. Current signals are scattered across decks, spreadsheets, and Slack threads which causes last-minute re-scopes and uneven resourcing.

Goal: Deliver a lightweight, cadence-driven readiness dashboard and playbook that lets PMs and leads quickly surface blockers, risk (traffic-light style), and re-prioritization decisions tied to company OKRs. The dashboard should be consumable in the weekly syncs and support automated nudges before cutover windows.

Success criteria (measurable):
- 75% of company-level initiative leads report the dashboard reduces prep time for leadership syncs by >=30% (survey, after 2 cycles).
- Reduce number of unplanned scope changes in the weekly cadence by 40% (tracking changes vs baseline).
- 95% of initiatives have a defined readiness state (green/amber/red) with supporting evidence attached.

Scope: MVP includes a view that maps company OKRs -> initiatives -> readiness state, a lightweight notes field per initiative, and an automated checklist for release gating. Do not build a full roadmap editor in this phase. Integrations: Redwood Console API for rollout metadata, links to current PRs in GitHub, and a simple CSV import for teams not yet onboarded.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Traffic-light readiness (green/amber/red) vs numeric scoring: traffic-light chosen for faster adoption and conversational clarity in leadership syncs; numeric scores can be added later if needed.
- Centralized source of truth vs federated feeds: start with centralized dashboard that surfaces links to owner-managed artifacts to avoid heavy migration work.
- Manual status updates vs auto-inference: MVP requires owners to set readiness to ensure accountability; telemetry-led suggestions will be added in phase 2.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Wireframes reviewed and approved by Design and Eng (link in attachments).
- Backend endpoints to fetch OKR->initiative mapping and write readiness state implemented and documented (API contract in Confluence).
- Console view implemented with filters (by OKR, by org, by readiness) and export to CSV.
- Playbook doc created describing cadence roles, update frequency, and escalation paths.
- Pilot run with Growth and Infra teams across one cadence completed; feedback captured and list of follow-ups created.

Rollout plan:
1) Kickoff + PRD (this ticket) -> 1 week.
2) Parallel design + backend API -> 2 weeks.
3) Console UI + QA -> 1 week.
4) Pilot (Growth + Infra) -> 1 cycle (2 weeks).
5) Iterate and scale to remaining orgs -> next 4 weeks.

Notes for engineering: prioritize read-only performance for leadership view; endpoint must support paging and reduce N+1 reads for initiatives referenced by multiple OKRs. Use existing rollout metadata schema to avoid new ingestion pipelines.

Open questions:
- Should readiness be tied to a single owner or allow multiple co-owners? (provisional answer: allow primary owner + observers).
- What fields count as acceptable evidence for a green state? (proposed: test coverage, infra capacity signoff, open PRs <=2).
- Do we want automated nudges via Slack before syncs? (phase 2, but design hooks now).
